sections.html:
Caldwell, the seat of Canyon County, sits about 24 miles west of Boise inside the Boise metro area, and ranks fifth in Idaho by population. The 2020 census counted 59,996 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 76,629. That much growth puts houses of every age on the market, and any buyer with a mortgage will look hard at the roof, wiring and plumbing.

Two school districts cover the city, Caldwell School District and Vallivue School District, and the Caldwell district is the smallest in Idaho by area. Buyers comparing houses will want to know which one serves a given address. Because Boise is so close, a job change anywhere in the Treasure Valley can put a Caldwell household on a moving deadline.

sections.h2: Summer heat, winter cold and irrigation
sections.html:
Caldwell has a semi-arid climate with about 11.1 inches of precipitation a year. August highs average 93.7 degrees Fahrenheit, and December lows average 22.3. Extremes run further: a recorded high of 112 and a recorded low of minus 34.

Those swings are hard on cooling equipment, roof surfaces, attic ventilation and any plumbing in crawlspaces or outbuildings. Fences take a beating too, and the city regulates them.

Rain is scarce, so lawns and gardens depend on irrigation water. Find out from the county or your irrigation district what your lot's water rights and delivery schedule are. Buyers often want that answer in writing.

Caldwell's Code Compliance Division, part of the Community Development Department, enforces city code on rubbish, weeds, vacant buildings, fences, signs and some business uses. An open violation can slow a sale. Walk the lot with this list in hand:

  • Waste material and personal property exposed to the elements and visible from public view must be cleared.
  • Vacant, open and accessible buildings must be boarded up and secured.
  • Weeds taller than eight inches must be cut or removed.
  • A business needs a city business license, and a home business needs a home occupation permit.
  • Fence maintenance and sign rules are enforced as well.

The division also enforces zoning. Some activities need approval from the Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing Examiner or the City Council.

If you inherited a house that has sat empty, clear the weeds and secure the doors before any inspection. The Building Safety Division handles permits and inspections, and its inspection request line is (208) 455-4605. If a prior owner built an addition or finished a garage without a permit, a buyer's lender may ask about it. Know the answer before you sign anything.

The county assessor values the property, the treasurer collects, and the same two due dates apply to every owner. Assessment notices for the regular roll go out in June, and the first half of the tax is due December 20, with the second half due June 20. When a date falls on a weekend, the county extends it. For 2026, the first half is due December 21, 2026, because the 20th is a Sunday.

One buyer question comes up often. If someone buys a home after April 15, they can still apply for the homeowner's exemption, but it counts toward the following tax year. The legislature picked April 15 because net taxable value has to freeze at a set point. If you sell in spring, remind your buyer to file in time for the next cycle.

Idaho's Property Condition Disclosure Act covers most home sales here. Section 55-2504 puts the duty on anyone about to transfer residential property, rentals the owner never occupied included. They complete the relevant items on the form described in section 55-2508.

Section 55-2505 lists who is excused. Fiduciaries handling an estate or trust, foreclosure transfers, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and heirs who have stayed out of the house for the last year all qualify. An exemption does not mean silence. A buyer can still inspect, and a seller who knows about a leaking roof or a failing septic system should think hard before saying nothing. A title company or an Idaho attorney can sort out your situation.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale right for your Caldwell house?
sections.html:
Sometimes. It suits owners who want to avoid repair bills, open houses and months on the market. A house that would not pass a buyer's loan inspection is a natural fit, and so is an inherited property or a rental with no tenant. Typical reasons for calling:

  • An inherited house is sitting empty and you want to head off code letters.
  • Deferred repairs would trip a loan inspection.
  • A move requires a firm closing date.
  • A rental has become more work than it is worth.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as they are, with no commissions and no closing costs charged to the seller by us. We do not promise a price here, and you can turn any offer down at no cost. If you want to compare methods, ask a real estate agent for a second opinion.

sections.h2: How a Caldwell cash sale runs
sections.html:
With no bank involved, the pace is set by your paperwork and the title search. First, describe the property to us: condition, liens, back taxes and who is living there. Next comes a written offer. Once you say yes, the title company clears the title, drafts the documents and books a closing on a day that suits you.

On closing day, any mortgage or tax balance is paid from your proceeds and you receive what is left. Request the settlement statement beforehand. The Canyon County treasurer can confirm what is owed, and the closing agent splits the year's tax between you and the buyer.

Nothing is binding until you sign. If a listing would leave you with more, or if a relative wants the house, take that route. Cash makes the most sense when the calendar or the condition of the property is the real obstacle, and when you would trade a possible higher price for a certain date.

1. Walk the lot against the code compliance list above.
  2. Find your assessment notice and note the district, the exemption status and the due dates.
  3. Ask the Building Safety Division about permits for any addition or conversion.
  4. Learn your lot's irrigation rights and schedule.
  5. Decide whether a listing or a cash offer matches your timeline.

With these answers in hand, calls to a buyer, a lender or a title officer go faster.

faqs.q: How many people live in Caldwell, Idaho?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 76,629 residents. The 2020 census counted 59,996.

faqs.q: When are Canyon County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due December 20 and the second half June 20. For 2026, the first half is due December 21 because the 20th falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: Can I get the homeowner's exemption if I buy a Caldwell house after April 15?
faqs.a: You can apply, but the exemption counts toward the next tax year. The legislature chose April 15 because net taxable value must freeze at a set point.

faqs.q: What code violations should I fix before selling a Caldwell house?
faqs.a: Caldwell enforces rules on rubbish, weeds over eight inches, open or unsecured vacant buildings, fences, signs and unlicensed home businesses. Clearing those before you list avoids delays.

faqs.q: Which school district is a Caldwell house in?
faqs.a: Caldwell is served by the Caldwell School District and the Vallivue School District. Confirm the district for a specific address with the district office.
